newsitem.title: KENYA: FOREIGN INVESTORS HOLD OFF NERVOUS NAIROBI BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN INVESTORS HOLD OFF NERVOUS NAIROBI BOURSE.

text.p: Foreign investors kept off the bond market at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) on Thursday discouraged by unattractive prices offered by market makers in a bid to stem a wave of panic-selling by nervous investors.
Bourse officials said a total of 7.85 million shillings (113,883) of the Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond from a record 400 million shillings sold on Wednesday.
"Market makers were offering an average price of 102.2 percent which is way below the 102.7 percent offered yesterday (Wednesday)," said a floor dealer from a top brokerage firm.

Anxious foreign investors flooded the equity market this week after the shilling plunged to record official lows in the aftermath of an International Monetary Fund ruling to halt a key aid package to Kenya in a row over corruption.
They offloaded a record turnover of bonds before buying hard currency to repatriate their profits or investments.

The shilling was quoted at a commercial average of 70.2 against the dollar at 2 p.m. (1100 GMT) from 68.55 at 0730 GMT and a closing rate of 67.50 on Wednesday. The shilling decline against the dollar from Thursday was 4.0 percent.

"The bond has fuelled the shilling's loss and foreign investors have partly contributed to the shilling's fall by asking commercial banks to look for dollars and not in small amounts -- even if it's still hurting them," a broker said.
"Today there were all the indications that they were going to offload but they chose to withhold after they saw the prices offered by market-maker," another broker said.

One commercial bank said they were buying the bonds at 102.2986 percent and 102.4213 percent for the third and fourth issue respectively compared to Wednesday's close of 102.5050 and 102.7 percent respectively.

The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index shed 5.49 points to close at 3421.16 points. Turnover was posted at 12.1 million shillings on 309,926 shares compared to 19.4 million shillings on 342,079 shares on Wednesday, floor dealers said.
